en: Now follows the Śrī Lakṣmaṇa Kavaca from within the glorious Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa.
Agastya said:
[Behold] the dark-complexioned son of Sumitrā, who gazes upon the pair of feet of the Leader of the Raghus and holds with his own hand a beautiful and excellent parasol over the head of Rāma.
I bow to that lotus-eyed one, who constantly holds the great bow of the Lord of the Raghus upon his bowstring and is ever intent upon the words of Janaka’s daughter.
Of this Śrī Lakṣmaṇa-kavaca mantra, Agastya is the seer (ṛṣi),
Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ),
and Śrī Lakṣmaṇa is the deity (devatā).
"Śeṣa" is the seed-syllable (bīja);
"Sumitrānandana" is the power (śakti);
"Rāmānuja" is the peg (kīlaka).
"Rāmadāsa" is the weapon;
"born of the Raghu lineage" is the armor;
and "Saumitri" is the mantra.
This is the application (viniyoga) for the purpose of pleasing Śrī Lakṣmaṇa and for the accomplishment of all desired objects.
Now follows the assignment of finger positions (aṅgulinyāsa).
Oṃ, to Lakṣmaṇa, salutation to the two thumbs; Oṃ, to Śeṣa, salutation to the two index fingers;
Oṃ, to the delighter of Sumitrā, salutation to the two middle fingers.
Oṃ, salutation to Rāmānuja with the two ring fingers;
Oṃ, salutation to Rāmadāsa with the two little fingers;
Oṃ, salutation to the one born of the Raghu lineage with the palms and backs of the hands.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other limbs.
Oṃ, homage to Lakṣmaṇa, the heart; Oṃ, svāhā to Śeṣa, the head;
Oṃ, vaṣaṭ to Sumitrānandana, the tuft of hair.
Oṃ, to Rāmānuja, the armor, huṃ! Oṃ, to the servant of Rāma, the three eyes, vauṣaṭ! Oṃ, to the one born of the Raghu lineage, the weapon, phaṭ!
Oṃ saumitraye; thus is the binding of the directions.
Now, meditation.
Seated upon the back of Rāma, beautiful, wearing jeweled earrings, dark as the petal of a blue lotus, and adorned with jeweled bracelets. || 1 ||
He bore a supreme, divine parasol over the head of Rāma;
he wore excellent yellow garments and was adorned with a crown. || 2 ||
He bore both quiver and bow, possessed a smiling countenance, wore a divine garland of jewels, and was resplendent with a flower garland. || 3 ||
Having meditated thus upon Lakṣmaṇa, whose eyes are cast down, O Rāghava,
men should then recite the armor-mantra (kavaca) here with devotion.

Oṃ! May Lakṣmaṇa protect me in the east; may the younger brother of Rāghava protect me in the south; may the son of Sumitrā protect me in the west; and may the best of the Raghus protect me in the north.
May Mahāvīra protect me from below, and may the Son of the King protect me from above;
may Rāmadāsa protect my middle, and may Satyapālaka protect me from all sides.
May he with the smiling face protect my head; may the husband of Ūrmilā protect my forehead;
may the wielder of the bow, the son of Sumitrā, protect the space between my eyebrows; and may he protect my right eye.
May Ramamantri always protect my cheeks;
may Kabandhabhujagaṇḍana always protect the roots of my ears.
May Sumitrā, the increaser of joy, always protect the tip of my nose;
may Rāma, whose eyes are ever-fixed upon her, always protect my face here on earth.
May he who carried out Sītā’s words always protect my speech here;
may he of gentle form protect my tongue, and may Ananta protect my teeth.
May the slayer of Rākṣasas protect my chin; may the destroyer of Asuras protect my throat;
may the conqueror of enemies protect my shoulders; and may the lotus-eyed one protect my arms.
May he who wears bracelets protect my hands; may Raktanakha protect my nails;
may Vinidra protect my belly; and may Jitendriya protect my chest. 12.
The beautiful one [protected] the sides; the one standing at the back protected the region of the back;
he with the deep navel protected the navel; and he with the golden girdle protected the hips.
May the thousand-faced one protect the secret parts; may he who is dear to Hari protect the genitals. May Viṣṇu’s couch protect the thighs; may Sumukha protect the knees.
May the Lord of Nāgas protect my shanks; may he who wears anklets protect my ankles; may Aṅgada protect my feet, and may Sulocana protect my limbs.
Thus ends the Śrī Lakṣmaṇa-kavaca within the Manohara-kāṇḍa of the glorious Ānanda-rāmāyaṇa of Vālmīki, which comprises one hundred million verses of the life of Rāma.
